today.h: The AI Trade Gave Back a Fifth of Monday: Nasdaq -1.48%, S&P -0.50%, Dow +0.85%
today.d: Nvidia's comeback faded in a session: NVDA -5.86%, the chip ETF -8.27% and Anthropic closed below its $83 IPO price, but the damage stayed inside megacap AI, so the Dow added 423 points and nine of 11 sectors rose.
today.c1: Nvidia's reinstatement rally lasted one session. The S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,201.09 (-36.08 points) and the Nasdaq Composite 1.48% to 23,733.54 (-356.02) as the AI complex that carried Monday's 4.73% surge was sold; the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.99%. Nvidia dropped 5.86% to $155.38, giving back about a fifth of Monday's 31.48% gain, while Micron fell 11.01%, AMD 8.86% and the iShares Semiconductor ETF 8.27%. Anthropic closed at $81.90, 6.54% lower and below the $83 price of last week's IPO. Analog Devices fell 17.37% after reporting late Monday, the worst S&P 500 performer, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise 16.31% despite a beat. The damage was contained: the Dow rose 423.39 points to 50,018.70, the Russell 2000 added 0.57%, nine of 11 sectors rose and health care led at +2.95%. The S&P sits 7.90% below its 10/6 record of 7,818.93.
today.c4:
• The trigger: Monday's 31% Nvidia rebound was a governance re-rating, not an earnings revision, and it reversed within a session; NVDA is still 35% below its 10/6 record close.
  • The tape: the S&P fell 0.50% while the Dow rose 0.85% and the Russell 2000 0.57%; the 48 largest companies accounted for -44.8 of the index's -36.1 points.
  • The rate backdrop: futures price a 95% probability of a 25bp December hike, which is why gold fell 2.45% and the 10Y could not rally.
  • The gate: October PCE on 11/25; US markets are closed 11/26 for Thanksgiving and close at 1 p.m. ET on 11/27.
  • The tell: whether chip losses stay inside AI hardware or start hitting the industrials and retailers that rallied on Tuesday.

chains.t: ⑤ Crude Bounced Off Three-Month Lows on Hormuz Attacks
steps: Brent for January settled up $2.03, or 2.27%, at $91.40, and WTI up $1.88, or 2.35%, at $82.05.
Brent's session low was $88.10, its weakest since August 27, and WTI's $79.07, its weakest since August 10.
A container ship was targeted on an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, after three vessels were hit by projectiles on 11/23.
The US is investigating whether Iran was behind cyberattacks on as many as 50 energy tankers, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Supply still caps the rally: Libya's Sharara pipeline reopened and Deutsche Bank put October's implied oversupply at 1.7 million barrels a day.
Kpler put Hormuz traffic 42% below prewar levels in the seven days through 11/21.
chains.d: Oil's bounce was a risk premium, not a shortage: tanker attacks lifted crude off three-month lows, but Brent is still 19.42% lower this month because supply is rebuilding faster than demand.

news.fact: Brent crude futures settled up $2.03, or 2.27%, to $91.40 a barrel; US West Texas Intermediate settled up $1.88, or 2.35%, at $82.05.
Brent bounced off a session trough that was its lowest since August 27, and its session low was $88.10 a barrel, while WTI slipped as low as $79.07, the weakest since August 10.
A container ship was targeted while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, according to state media.
Three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles on Monday as they sailed east through the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday.
The US is investigating whether Iran was involved in cyberattacks on as many as 50 energy tankers, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials.
Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has reopened, and Deutsche Bank said global observed liquids inventories rose in October, implying an oversupply of 1.7 million barrels per day.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained 42% below prewar levels in the seven days through Nov. 21, according to preliminary data from Kpler.

mtd.c1: November is a 5.00% drawdown on the S&P 500 from the 10/30 base of 7,580.07, and its shape has not changed: the month's high was 7,688.62 on 11/4, its low 6,910.39 on 11/20, and the last two sessions recovered 41.6% of the 10.12% slide from that high, 4.21 percentage points. Technology (-12.49%) and energy (-13.67%) are the two worst of the 11 sectors; communications (+4.55%), staples (+2.75%), consumer discretionary (+2.03%) and real estate (+0.67%) are the only ones above the line. The Nasdaq is 6.70% lower for the month against the Dow's 3.38%, and the S&P is 7.90% below its 10/6 record.
mtd.c4:
• The shape: AI and oil took the month down; the 11/20 low was 8.83% below the base before two sessions cut that to 5.00%.
  • The breadth: four of 11 sectors are above the 10/30 line, and two of them are defensives.
  • The hedge that failed: gold -8.64%, bitcoin -22.75% and Brent -19.42% all lost money while the VIX rose 35.74%.
  • The rates: the 2Y rose 7bp while the 10Y fell 3bp, a 10bp flattening to 28bp.
  • The next test: October PCE on 11/25, then the December FOMC that the market has already priced for a hike.

qtd.h: Q4 Is a 5.89% Drawdown With a Bond Bid
qtd.d: Q4 has taken the S&P 5.89% below its 9/30 base and the Nasdaq 11.64%, while the 10Y has fallen 38bp: an AI de-rating with a bond rally, not a rate shock.
qtd.c1: Q4 is a 5.89% drawdown on the S&P 500 from the 9/30 base of 7,651.54 and an 11.64% drawdown on the Nasdaq, while the Dow is only 1.74% lower. The quarter's low was 6,910.39 on 11/20, 9.69% below the base; the last two sessions recovered 41.6% of that drawdown, 4.21 percentage points. Technology is 19.75% lower for the quarter and communications 5.88% lower, while staples +14.00%, utilities +10.04%, health +9.68% and consumer discretionary +8.16% lead: seven of 11 sectors are higher. The 10Y fell 38bp over the same window, so the de-rating came with a bond bid rather than a rate shock.
qtd.c4:
• The shape: an AI de-rating inside an equity drawdown, with the Dow down only 1.74% against the Nasdaq's 11.64%.
  • The rates: 10Y -38bp, 30Y -34bp and 2Y -25bp; 2s10s flattened 41bp to 28bp.
  • The rotation: seven of 11 sectors are higher, led by staples and utilities.
  • The commodity side: gold -14.92%, bitcoin -28.62% and Brent -3.30% on a roll-adjusted basis.
  • The carry: the 2Y is still 116bp above its 2026 starting point even after this quarter's 25bp give-back — the year's bill, not the quarter's.

ytd.h: The Year Is Still Positive: S&P +5.19%, Nasdaq +2.11%
ytd.d: 2026 has round-tripped: the S&P is 5.19% above its 12/31 base after being 14.22% higher at the 10/6 record, the Nasdaq is only 2.11% higher, and the 10Y sits 73bp above where the year started.
ytd.c1: 2026 is still a positive year, but barely for the AI index. The S&P 500 is 5.19% above its 12/31 base of 6,845.50 after being 14.22% higher at the 10/6 record of 7,818.93, and it is now 7.90% below that record. The Nasdaq is 2.11% higher after leading the first nine months; energy +35.20%, health +19.33% and staples +18.28% are the year's leaders, while communications -11.27% is the only double-digit loser. The 10Y is 73bp higher at 4.91%, with the 2Y up 116bp, and gold is 17.94% lower: the year's gains survived the quarter, but the leadership rotated.
ytd.c4:
• The round trip: S&P +14.22% at the 10/6 record is now +5.19%, a 9.03-point give-back.
  • The leadership: energy, health and staples replaced AI at the top of the year's return table.
  • The rates: the front end is 116bp higher and the 2s10s spread has flattened from 71bp to 28bp.
  • The stores of value: gold -17.94% and bitcoin -31.85%, the year's worst assets.
  • The base case: the year is positive because earnings and defensives held; AI still adds, with tech +9.11% against the S&P's +5.19%, but it no longer leads.
